summary: Intermittent throughput throttling during predictive prewarm failure and noise-isolation lapse
description: Issue summary: Multiple dedicated-tenant customers (notably ScribeAI) observed sudden p99 throughput drops during the midday predictive prewarm window. The regression appears as short (2–8 minute) bouts of severe request throttling and queuing on reserved GPU pools, causing inference latency to spike and tail-off in throughput. Impact: Several customers experienced degraded UX in customer-facing flows (chat and embedding pipelines) with 30–60% reduced throughput at p95/p99 and visible client-side timeouts for long-lived streams. Environment: prod-us-east and prod-eu-west dedicated pools, predictive-prewarm enabled, autoscale predictive window 11:30–12:30 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Enable predictive prewarm for a small dedicated customer pool; 2) Run a mixed stream workload (50% short streams, 50% long streams) with ramp to 200 qps; 3) Observe autoscaler prewarm allocations and slot attach logs; 4) During prewarm completion window, send steady background low-CPU health-check streams. Observed behavior: - Autoscaler attempts prewarm allocations but several gpus remain in "allocating" state and do not attach slots for 1–3 minutes. - When allocations finally attach, there's immediate slot serialization: bursts of tiny short streams interleave with long streams producing KV-cache thrash and GPU memory spike; - Platform emits transient "noisy-tenant-eviction" and "slot-attach-timeout" warnings; - Throughput drops even after prewarm completes due to background eviction sweep kicking in. Expected behavior: Prewarm should bring pools to steady-state capacity without introducing eviction sweeps or slot attach timeouts; slot attach time should remain <15s; throughput should ramp without p99 regressions. Logs/metrics referenced: allocator logs (alloc-cycle-2026-03-12T11:29), autoscaler event timeline, per-GPU nvlink/io wait charts, KV-cache size heatmap. Temporary mitigation applied: disabled predictive prewarm for affected pools and applied a short noise-isolation rule (per-tenant short-stream cap) which recovered throughput to baseline within 6 minutes. Next steps: deep-dive autoscaler prewarm/attach path and eviction sweep heuristics; investigate background daemon that triggers eviction sweeps during attach windows; propose a canary change to defer eviction during prewarm window.

investigation_notes: Checked allocator logs: repeated 'slot-attach-timeout' entries at 11:31–11:38 UTC; attach timeouts correlated with increased kernel queue depth on GPUs 2/3 of node.gpu-77 cluster.
KV-cache heatmap shows rapid growth followed by GC spikes exactly at attach retry timestamps; cache growth caused memory pressure and triggered eviction daemon.

Autoscaler event trace: prewarm allocation created, health-check streams started immediately, which kept tiny connections open and increased multiplexing overhead; background eviction daemon has threshold 'inactive-time-seconds' set to 30s which is too low for attach windows.
Network telemetry: no packet loss between control plane and node, but slightly elevated TLS handshake latencies during the period (likely due to node kernel context switching under IO pressure).

Staging repro: synthetic small-stream fanout + predictive prewarm reproduced attach timeout and eviction interplay at lower scale; confirms behavioral hypothesis rather than customer workload peculiarity.
Related PRs: autoscaler backoff change under review (github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/112) and allocator attach metrics instrumented (github.com/redwood/realtime-allocator/pull/389).
Cross-check: linked incident SUP-900998 had similar attach-timeout signals but from a different root (training jobs on the same cluster); suggests need for better isolation of prewarm window.
Impact quant: ScribeAI - p99 latency increased from 220ms to 1.9s; throughput (requests/min) dropped by ~48% during incident window.
resolution_notes: Emergency mitigation: predictive prewarm disabled for affected tenant pools and a temporary short-stream cap applied to reduce KV-cache thrash. Post-mitigation monitoring shows return to baseline throughput. Planned permanent fix: implement 'prewarm lock' to pause eviction sweeps during prewarm attach windows, increase attach retry backoff, and add an autoscaler feature-flag to avoid prewarm when background eviction load is detected. Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC to 5% of dedicated pools, with rollback on p99 degradation. Follow-ups: update prewarm runbook, add alert for 'attach-timeout rate' and 'eviction-during-prewarm' composite signal, and coordinate with capacity planning to ensure prewarm nodes are not co-located with heavy background jobs. Estimated resolution ETA after canary: 5 business days.
